# We're campaigning for free software. We need your help — Free Software Foundation — Working together for free software

## We're campaigning for free software. We need your help

I'm Greg Farough, the campaigns manager of the [Free Software
Foundation (FSF)](https://fsf.org). If you haven't heard from me in a while, it's
because the [campaigns team](https://fsf.org/campaigns) has been heads-down in researching the
latest threats to software freedom and promoting *real* digital rights
all over the globe. We've been particularly concerned with the glut of
age verification bills springing up all over the United States and
elsewhere; proposed bans on VPNs; and the ongoing, more general
encroachment of proprietary software on all of our basic freedoms.
We've also been preparing for this year's [International Day Against
DRM](https://defectivebydesign.org) on July 17th. We do all of this to educate the public about
free software; caution them against the latest "offerings" from Apple,
Microsoft, and Google; steer them away from streaming dis-services; defend their privacy; and
more. That amounts to [sixteen(!)](https://fsf.org/campaigns) campaigns with just three
full-time staff members.

The fight can seem overwhelming, especially in the wake of one
specific social media titan and proprietary software slinger recently
becoming the world's first trillionaire. What do three people at a
small Massachusetts-based nonprofit have to compare against that? The
answer is our principles.

For decades, the FSF has stuck to its message that users should be
able to have [full control](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html) over their machines. We cannot allow
these freedoms to be limited based on anyone's age, location, sexual
orientation, migration status, or any other characteristic some suit
on a senate floor determines to be a good method of censoring the
populace and limiting access to technology. Digital discrimination to
any such extent is possible only with proprietary software.

We haven't departed from our principles — not once — and have instead
been elaborating on the core message and implications for the last
forty-one years. When it seems like each and every corporate monopoly
around the world is in a race to shut down every meaningful way to
copy, study, or even *run* the programs that power our digital lives,
rest assured that the FSF is here to defend your right to compute.

But we can't do it alone. Since joining the FSF in 2019, I've seen my
fair share of threats to free software come and go — but none have
made me more worried about the future of free software than recent
device-based age verification laws. Meaningful advocacy for software
freedom requires funding. Your associate membership directly impacts
the amount of work that Eko, Heshan, and I can do for the free
software movement. In short, we need your help.

We know not everyone is in a position to give, but if you can, support
our efforts by joining the FSF as an [associate member](https://my.fsf.org/join?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=campaigns). For $70
annually or $12 monthly, you can support our campaigning for a year.
This isn't just about finances; it's about showing up in numbers.
Please help us continue to protect software freedom and increase its
global support. Every membership this summer will help us towards our
goal of 175 new members. Associate members will also be able to enjoy
all the [member benefits](https://www.fsf.org/associate/benefits?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=campaigns).

There's something I've learned in my time working here and being
involved with the free software movement generally. Nowhere else have
I seen a community of such principled, dedicated people all together
in one place and standing up for human liberty in technology. If
anyone can turn the fate of the digital world around, it's this
community.

Please join me in committing to freedom and supporting the FSF.

#### Document Actions

- **[Share on social networks](https://www.fsf.org/share?u=https://www.fsf.org/blogs/community/2026-were-campaigning-for-free-software&t=We're campaigning for free software. We need your help)**
- [News](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/news.xml)
- [Events](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/events.xml)
- [Blogs](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/blogs.xml)
- [Jobs](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/jobs.xml)
- [GNU](http://www.gnu.org/rss/whatsnew.rss)

# 我們正在為自由軟體倡議。我們需要你的幫助 — 自由軟體基金會 — 共同為自由軟體努力

## 我們正在為自由軟體倡議。我們需要你的幫助

我是 Greg Farough，[自由軟體基金會（Free Software Foundation, FSF）](https://fsf.org)的倡議活動經理。如果你有一陣子沒收到我的消息，那是因為[倡議團隊](https://fsf.org/campaigns)一直埋頭研究軟體自由面臨的最新威脅，並在全球各地推動*真正的*數位權利。我們特別關切美國各地與其他地方大量冒出的年齡驗證法案、擬議中的 VPN 禁令，以及專有軟體對我們所有基本自由持續且更廣泛的侵蝕。我們也一直在準備今年 7 月 17 日的[國際反 DRM 日](https://defectivebydesign.org)。我們做這些事，是為了讓大眾認識自由軟體；提醒他們小心 Apple、Microsoft 和 Google 最新的「產品」；讓他們遠離有害的串流服務；捍衛他們的隱私；以及更多工作。這加起來共有[十六（！）](https://fsf.org/campaigns)項倡議活動，而全職工作人員只有三位。

這場戰鬥有時看起來令人難以招架，尤其是在某位社群媒體巨頭兼專有軟體販售者最近成為世界上第一位兆萬富翁之後。位在麻薩諸塞州的一個小型非營利組織裡，三個人要拿什麼和那樣的力量相比？答案是我們的原則。

數十年來，FSF 一直堅守同一個訊息：使用者應該能夠對自己的機器擁有[完整控制權](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html)。我們不能允許這些自由因任何人的年齡、所在地、性傾向、移民身分，或參議院議場上某個穿西裝的人認定適合用來審查民眾、限制技術取得的任何其他特徵而受到限制。這種程度的數位歧視，只有在專有軟體之下才可能發生。

我們從未背離自己的原則，一次也沒有；相反地，過去四十一年來，我們一直在闡明這個核心訊息及其意涵。當全球每一個企業壟斷巨頭似乎都在競相封鎖所有真正有意義的方式，讓人無法複製、研究，甚至*執行*那些支撐我們數位生活的程式時，請放心，FSF 會在這裡捍衛你的運算權利。

但我們無法獨自完成這件事。自從 2019 年加入 FSF 以來，我看過不少對自由軟體的威脅來來去去；但沒有任何一項，比最近以裝置為基礎的年齡驗證法，更讓我擔憂自由軟體的未來。要真正倡議軟體自由，就需要資金支持。你的準會員身份，會直接影響 Eko、Heshan 和我能為自由軟體運動投入多少工作。簡單說，我們需要你的幫助。

我們知道不是每個人都有能力捐款，但如果你可以，請透過加入 FSF 成為[準會員](https://my.fsf.org/join?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=campaigns)來支持我們的努力。每年 70 美元或每月 12 美元，就能支持我們一整年的倡議工作。這不只是財務問題；也關乎展現人數上的支持。請幫助我們持續保護軟體自由，並提升它在全球的支持度。今年夏天每一位加入的會員，都會幫助我們朝新增 175 位會員的目標前進。準會員也能享有所有[會員福利](https://www.fsf.org/associate/benefits?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=campaigns)。

在這裡工作、也參與自由軟體運動的這段時間裡，我學到了一件事。我從沒在其他地方見過一個社群，能聚集這麼多如此有原則、如此投入的人，一同為科技領域中的人類自由挺身而出。如果有誰能扭轉數位世界的命運，那就是這個社群。

請和我一起承諾自由，並支持 FSF。

#### 文件操作

- **[分享到社群網路](https://www.fsf.org/share?u=https://www.fsf.org/blogs/community/2026-were-campaigning-for-free-software&t=We're campaigning for free software. We need your help)**
- [新聞](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/news.xml)
- [活動](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/events.xml)
- [部落格](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/blogs.xml)
- [徵才](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/jobs.xml)
- [GNU](http://www.gnu.org/rss/whatsnew.rss)
